pr_body:
writeTextString no longer uses ResolveBlankPaddedChar which was causing an increase in heap allocations mainly due to it's use of `make([]byte, t.Width())`.  Additionally in this PR I removed the call to ResolveBlankPaddedChar from writeBinaryString and other occurences in types.go.

These are the results that we now see from benchmark tests:

Micro Benchmark:
```
                      │   sec/op    │   sec/op     vs base               │
WriteTextColumnarChar   41.49µ ± 2%   24.05µ ± 3%  -42.03% (p=0.001 n=7)

                      │  before.txt  │              after.txt              │
                      │     B/op     │    B/op      vs base                │
WriteTextColumnarChar   16.00Ki ± 0%   0.00Ki ± 0%  -100.00% (p=0.001 n=7)

                      │ before.txt  │              after.txt              │
                      │  allocs/op  │  allocs/op   vs base                │
WriteTextColumnarChar   1.024k ± 0%   0.000k ± 0%  -100.00% (p=0.001 n=7)
```

Sysbench:
```
                                        │ sys_gce_before.txt │         sys_gce_after.txt         │
                                        │       sec/op       │   sec/op     vs base              │
Sysbench/SQL/1node_local/oltp_read_only          7.313m ± 4%   7.071m ± 4%  -3.32% (p=0.009 n=6)

                                        │ sys_gce_before.txt │         sys_gce_after.txt          │
                                        │        B/op        │     B/op      vs base              │
Sysbench/SQL/1node_local/oltp_read_only         972.3Ki ± 2%   895.3Ki ± 1%  -7.92% (p=0.002 n=6)

                                        │ sys_gce_before.txt │         sys_gce_after.txt          │
                                        │     allocs/op      │  allocs/op   vs base               │
Sysbench/SQL/1node_local/oltp_read_only          6.179k ± 4%   5.250k ± 2%  -15.03% (p=0.002 n=6)
```

Epic: CRDB-42584
Fixes: #134336
Release note: None

issue_context.body:
Extracted from https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/134274.

In https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/132338, we eliminated the call to `ResolveBlankPaddedCharBytes` from `writeBinaryBytes`, opting to instead pad directly in the `writeBuffer`. We should do the same for the text protocol by eliminting the call to `ResolveBlankPaddedChar` in `writeTextString`.

Jira issue: CRDB-44025

Epic CRDB-42584

review_comments: Padding is type-specific, so the logic for adding it made more sense being in the `types.go` file, not a method of the more general `writeBuffer`. Consider refactoring it back to what it was.

Thanks Marcus! I went ahead and made this change in this PR https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/136118
<!-- Reviewable comment -OCZBDfH9OKqDZ7ZZcIP:b-4gu4dn -->
<!-- Sent from Reviewable.io -->

In the general case, a `string` to `[]byte` cast requires an allocation. In this particular case, Go is able to optimize away the allocation. But avoiding the `[]byte` casts altogether would be safer against future regressions and more obvious to readers that no allocations are occurring. If that requires some code duplication, I think it is well worth it. Can you try to rework these changes with that in mind?

Thanks Marcus! I went ahead and made this change in this PR https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/136118
<!-- Reviewable comment -OCZJ0TlEFHfAz2AxCpC:b-4gu4dn -->
<!-- Sent from Reviewable.io -->

This now looks like two separate code paths, whereas before it was clearer to see that writing bytes with or without padding was done exactly the same, besides the additional step to add padding if necessary. If your goal was to encapsulate some of the logic in named functions, one compromise would be something like:

```go
pad := paddingForStringType(len(v), t)
b.putInt23(int32(len(v) + pad))
b.write(v)
for pad > 0 {
    n := min(pad, len(spaces))
    b.write(spaces[:n])
    pad -= n
}
```

Thanks Marcus! I will address this in this PR: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/136118
